issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String): void (an int plus a reason String), but the solution implements addGuestStudents with a single int parameter only. This signature mismatch contradicts the specified API and may confuse students about the required parameters and behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the addGuestStudents method signature in the solution match the specification: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason). Ensure the method accepts the reason parameter (and either stores, logs, or documents it) while still updating numberOfGuestStudents. Alternatively, update the problem statement and UML if the reason parameter was not intended.

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) requires a method addGuestStudents(int, String) that accepts a number of new guest students and a String reason. The solution implements addGuestStudents(int) without the String reason parameter. The template leaves a TODO and does not provide a concrete signature. This mismatch in the method signature for the same conceptual operation will confuse students about the required method API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution (and template) with the problem statement by implementing addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) in Lecture. Update the method body to record or use the reason (or document why the reason is ignored). Alternatively, if the reason parameter is not needed pedagogically, update the problem statement and UML to specify addGuestStudents(int) to avoid the discrepancy.
